title: NGO & Society Registration in Bangladesh: 1860 Act & NGOAB Guide
metaTitle: NGO & Society Registration BD: 1860 Act & NGOAB
metaDescription: How to register an NGO, foundation, or society in Bangladesh: Societies Act 1860 (RJSC), Section 28 non-profit company, Social Services (DSS) & NGOAB FD-1.
heroIntro: Non-profit foundations, professional associations, and development NGOs in Bangladesh can incorporate under multiple legal vehicles—most commonly a Society under the Societies Registration Act 1860 (at RJSC), a Voluntary Social Welfare Organization (at DSS), a Section 28 Non-Profit Company, or a Registered Trust. However, receiving any foreign grant or donation triggers mandatory NGO Affairs Bureau (NGOAB) registration under the Foreign Donations (Voluntary Activities) Regulation Act 2016.

quickAnswer.heading: At a Glance: Non-Profit & NGO Registration in Bangladesh
quickAnswer.text: Choose between RJSC Society, DSS Social Welfare, Section 28 Company, or Trust—then seek NGOAB approval for foreign funds.
points: RJSC Society (1860 Act): Requires minimum 7 founding members; ideal for associations, chambers, cultural & charitable societies
Section 28 Non-Profit Company: Licensed by Commerce Ministry / RJSC; zero dividend distribution, strong corporate governance
Department of Social Services (DSS): Local community welfare registration under the 1961 Ordinance
Foreign Funds Gatekeeper (NGOAB): Mandatory FD-1 registration & FD-6 project approval under the 2016 Act before spending foreign grants

sections.h2: Comparing the Four Legal Entities: Society vs. Section 28 vs. DSS vs. Trust
sections.content:
Before drafting founding documents, founders must match the entity type to their operational scope and donor expectations:

Legal StructureGoverning Statute & AuthorityMinimum FoundersBest Used For
Registered SocietySocieties Registration Act 1860 (RJSC)7 personsProfessional associations, alumni clubs, education/charity foundations
Non-Profit CompanySection 28, Companies Act 1994 (RJSC & Commerce Ministry)2 directors / membersLarge foundations, policy institutes, hospitals & chambers
Social Welfare OrgVoluntary Social Welfare Agencies Ordinance 1961 (DSS)7–11 membersGrassroots community charity, youth/women welfare
Charitable TrustTrusts Act 1882 & Registration Act 1908 (Sub-Registry)Settlor + 3–5 trusteesFamily endowments, scholarship & mosque/school trusts

sections.h2: Step-by-Step Society Registration at RJSC Under the 1860 Act
sections.content:
1. Name Clearance at RJSC: Apply online for name clearance ensuring the proposed Society name does not duplicate existing organizations or use restricted words improperly.
  2. Memorandum of Association & Constitution: Draft the Memorandum specifying objectives limited to Section 20 charitable, literary, scientific, or educational purposes, plus Bye-Laws governing General Body meetings, Executive Committee (EC) elections, and asset dissolution clauses (requiring remaining assets to pass to a similar society).
  3. Security Clearance & Filing: RJSC forwards founding details for Special Branch / Home Ministry verification as required; upon clearance and statutory fee payment, the Certificate of Registration is issued.

sections.h2: NGOAB Registration (Form FD-1) Under the Foreign Donations Act 2016
sections.content:
A common compliance mistake is assuming an RJSC or DSS certificate authorizes receiving foreign donor money. Under the Foreign Donations (Voluntary Activities) Regulation Act 2016:

  • Strict Prohibition Without FD-1: No NGO or society may receive or utilize foreign donations, grants, or crowdfunding transfers from abroad without prior NGO Affairs Bureau (NGOAB) registration (Form FD-1), valid for 10 years.
  • Project-by-Project Clearance (FD-6): Even after NGOAB registration, each funded project requires specific project approval via Form FD-6 before withdrawing grant funds from the designated Mother Bank Account.
  • Local-Fund Eligibility: Organizations relying purely on domestic Zakat, member subscriptions, or local corporate CSR do not require NGOAB clearance unless foreign funds enter their account.

Non-profits operating savings/loan programs must additionally obtain a license from the Microcredit Regulatory Authority (MRA) under the MRA Act 2006; unlicensed lending carries criminal penalties. Simultaneously, every registered society must obtain an e-TIN, submit audited annual financial statements to RJSC (Section 4), file annual NBR income tax returns under the Income Tax Act 2023, and apply separately for charitable tax exemption where eligible.

sections.h2: Essential Documents Checklist for Founding Members
sections.content:
• Certified Name Clearance printout from RJSC portal.
  • Signed Memorandum of Association and Rules & Regulations adopted by all 7+ founding members.
  • National ID (NID) / Passport copies, TIN certificates, and photographs of all Executive Committee members.
  • Proof of registered head office (tenancy agreement or ownership deed + utility bill).
  • Minutes of the first General Meeting approving the Constitution and electing the first Executive Committee.

faqs.q: How long does it take to register a Society with RJSC in Bangladesh?
faqs.a: Drafting and filing take 1 to 2 weeks, while overall issuance usually takes 2 to 4 months depending on Home Ministry / Special Branch verification timelines.

faqs.q: Can foreign citizens sit on the Executive Committee of a Bangladeshi Society or NGO?
faqs.a: Foreign nationals may serve as trustees, advisors, or members subject to security clearance; however, for NGOAB registration and smooth bank compliance, a majority Bangladeshi Executive Committee is strongly recommended.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a Society and a Section 28 Non-Profit Company?
faqs.a: A Section 28 company has corporate perpetual succession under the Companies Act 1994 and requires Ministry of Commerce licensing before RJSC incorporation, whereas an 1860 Act Society is simpler to form with 7 members directly at RJSC.
